family.toshiba-t-series.description: Toshiba’s T-series LCD laptops and plasma transportables, with distinct platforms and regional variants.
family.toshiba-t-series.history:
Toshiba’s T-series shows two ways of taking personal computing away from the desk: LCD laptops intended for mobility, and transportables bringing desktop performance to a case with an integrated screen. The numbering defines neither a shared architecture nor a linear succession; regional variants and suffixes retain their identities.

The T1100 went on sale in Europe in April 1985. PC/XT compatibility, an LCD and battery operation helped move office applications elsewhere, without implying that later laptops shared its board or design. The 1986 T3100 took another direction: an 80286, built-in hard disk and plasma display, with greater performance in a much heavier package.

The T3200 and T5100 continued that transportable approach. The original T3200 combines a 286 with EGA/AGS graphics; the T5100 brought the line to the 386 in 1987. Orange plasma is not an LCD with a backlight: it emits its own light. Display controls and conversion of colours into intensity levels shape each model’s experience. The T5200 added VGA and a sixteen-level panel; T3200SX and T5200C are hardware-different variants, not merely profiles of the originals.

Japanese documentation relates T5100 to J-3100SGT, but does not establish identical ROMs, keyboards or media. Service manuals, a BIOS date or a suffix alone cannot date a variant’s launch. The table retains known dates, reference periods and unresolved dates.

In this alpha, T3200, T5100 and T5200 have sheets and experimental creation. Each lists its limitations; T5100 uses compatibility video firmware because its original AGS ROM is still missing. Other names provide historical context, not a promise of available emulation.
